clinical_note:
SUBJECTIVE: The patient is a 58-year-old male presenting for a follow-up encounter regarding hyperlipidemia (disorder). He has a history including limited social contact, stress, and medication review due. Active medications include Acetaminophen 325 MG / Oxycodone Hydrochloride 10 MG Oral Tablet. Simvastatin 10 MG Oral Tablet was newly started and then stopped on the date of this encounter.

OBJECTIVE:
Laboratory results:
- Glucose [Mass/volume] in Blood: 70.2 mg/dL
- Urea nitrogen [Mass/volume] in Blood: 8.3 mg/dL
- Creatinine [Mass/volume] in Blood: 2.8 mg/dL
- Calcium [Mass/volume] in Blood: 10.0 mg/dL
- Sodium [Moles/volume] in Blood: 137.9 mmol/L
- Potassium [Moles/volume] in Blood: 4.4 mmol/L
- Chloride [Moles/volume] in Blood: 110.0 mmol/L
- Carbon dioxide total [Moles/volume] in Blood: 26.9 mmol/L
- Glomerular filtration rate: 82.5 mL/min
- Protein [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma: 7.7 g/dL
- Albumin [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma: 4.5 g/dL
- Globulin [Mass/volume] in Serum by calculation: 2.2 g/dL
- Bilirubin total [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma: 0.6 mg/dL
- Alkaline phosphatase: 89.8 U/L
- Alanine aminotransferase: 37.2 U/L

ASSESSMENT: Hyperlipidemia (disorder). Follow-up on lab work and medication management.

PLAN: Review lab results including elevated creatinine of 2.8 mg/dL. Discussed medication adjustments; Simvastatin 10 MG Oral Tablet was initiated and stopped on the same day. Continue current regimen of Acetaminophen / Oxycodone as needed.
dialogue:
[doctor] Hello. We are following up today on your hyperlipidemia and reviewing your recent lab work. How have you been feeling overall, especially with the stress and limited social contact we noted previously?
[patient] I have been dealing with some ongoing stress, but I came in to review my labs and talk about my cholesterol medication.
[doctor] Looking at your blood work from today, your glucose is 70.2 mg/dL, and your creatinine is elevated at 2.8 mg/dL, though your liver enzymes and electrolytes look fairly stable.
[patient] Is that creatinine level something we need to worry about? I am still taking my Percocet for pain management as well.
[doctor] Yes, we will keep a close eye on your kidney function given that creatinine level. Regarding your hyperlipidemia, we started you on Simvastatin 10 milligrams today, but we are also stopping it today based on our review.
[patient] Understood. So we are holding off on the simvastatin for now?
[doctor] Exactly. We will monitor everything closely and have you return for another follow-up to track your progress.
[patient] Sounds good, doctor. I will keep managing my pain with the acetaminophen and oxycodone and watch how I feel.

clinical_note: CHIEF COMPLAINT: Sepsis. HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: A 22-year-old male presenting to the emergency department with severe acute symptoms relating to sepsis. Patient was found to have positive blood cultures and clinical signs of systemic illness. PHYSICAL EXAM & VITALS: Initial vitals show oxygen saturation at 93.0% in arterial blood, mean blood pressure 89.6 mm[Hg], lactate 1.1 mmol/L, and physical exam notable for increased capillary filling time in the nail bed. ED COURSE & WORKUP: Blood cultures confirmed positive gram-positive blood culture panel by probe. Patient underwent resuscitation using intravenous fluid and was administered piperacillin 2000 MG / tazobactam 250 MG injection along with vancomycin 5 MG/ML injection. Due to clinical status, patient was subsequently transferred to the stepdown unit and later experienced episodes requiring ICU admission and repeated fluid resuscitations with fluctuating lactate levels (ranging up to 3.8 mmol/L) and blood pressures. DISPOSITION: Admitted for ongoing inpatient management of sepsis and septic shock with close monitoring.

[patient] Whatever you need to do, please help me. I haven't felt this sick before. [doctor] We are going to start you on intravenous fluids for resuscitation, along with intravenous antibiotics including piperacillin-tazobactam and vancomycin. [patient] Okay, will I need to stay in the hospital for this? [doctor] Yes, we will monitor your oxygen saturation and blood pressure closely, and you will be transferred to our stepdown unit for close observation after your initial treatment. [patient] Thank you, doctor. I appreciate you taking care of me.
